To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanisms mediating Ang II- or endothelin-induced constriction of renal afferent arteriolar smooth muscle cells (SMCs) are different from those of afferent efferent arteriular SMCs.

Ang II- and ET-induced constriction in AAs is mediated, in part, by a calcium channel-dependent mechanism, whereas Ang II- and, in particular, ET-induced constriction is mediated in EAs by a calcium channel-independent mechanism.

1) Ang II and ET induce AA constriction through a calcium-dependent mechanism that is sensitive to protein kinase C inhibition, whereas EA constriction induced either peptide is calcium-independent; and 2) the mechanisms mediating AA and EA constriction by Ang II and ET are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of isra-dipine on the constriction of AAs and EAs induced by Ang II and ET.
the mechanisms mediating renal vasoconstrictor responses to Ang II and ET.
the mechanisms mediating renal vascular constriction by Ang II and ET.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism of renal vasocontriction induced by Ang II and ET is different.
the mechanisms by which angiotensin (Ang) II and endothelin (Et) induce renal vasoconstrictions are similar, but not identical.
Ang II and ET cause renal vasoconstriciton by activating calcium channels in both AA and EA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the calcium channel as a major determinant of Ang II- and ET-induced constriction in AAs.
Ang II- and ET-induced constriction in the renal microvasculature is dependent on the activation of Ca2+ channels.
Ang II-induced renal vasoconstrictions were sensitive to calcium channel antagonists, and the sensitivity was dependent on the site of constriction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the calcium channels involved in mediating the vasoconstriction induced by angiotension II and endothelin are not identical and that the mechanisms mediating the vasaconstriction induced by these peptides are not identical.
protein kinase C and calcium channels play different roles in Ang II and endothelin-induced vasoconstriction in different segments of the microvasculature.
Ang II and endothelin induce renal microvascular vasoconstriction through activation of calcium channels, which are located primarily on the smooth muscle cells of the afferent arteriolar wall.
